verdict.rationale: First-party docs claim Angular is 'trusted by millions to build fast, reliable applications that scale with the size of your team' via fine-grained Signals reactivity, modular DI/components, and CLI tooling for testing/linting/caching (angular-docs-1,2,6,20). A Google engineer corroborates that >100k SLOC internal apps stay maintainable if the style guide is followed, and another dev reports a 170-view/100-controller SaaS app worked well with performance fixes (angular-comm-11,12), while independent benchmarks show optimized Angular matching or beating other frameworks (angular-comm-19). However, older community reports flag real scaling pain points (digest-cycle slowdowns, unclear guidance) mostly tied to legacy AngularJS rather than modern signal-based Angular. Missing for 10: recent independent large-scale case studies or benchmarks specific to current Angular (post-Ivy/Signals) versions, and clearer first-party guidance/tooling proof for team-scale maintainability beyond style guide mentions.
